interfaces.name: Relative food mass assay
interfaces.function: Prepare real comparison equipment, calibrate with retained stone pieces, and measure relative mass loss during real passive drying. Chemical screening is unavailable pending independently verified dependencies and implementation.
interfaces.costs: prepare-balance: target owned branch; controls explicitly allocate one vine stack, one bark stack, and two separate hard-stone items (first retained hammer, second 1-unit subdivision source); consumes 1 branch, 1 vine, 0.4 bark into balance, conserves 1 stone as five retained comparison pieces. Four assembly + two subdivision + three calibration rounds, 7.5 energy. prepare-dryer: target bark, controls [], apparatus empty; consumes 0.4 bark, two rounds and 1 energy. Empty apparatus for construction. Placement requires clear supported ground 0.65 east of performer. dry-mass: owned target, explicit balance apparatus, controls one retained calibrated weight, optional exact-tenths sample quantity (default 0.1); exactly one reachable tray. Preparation and each weighing cost 0.5 energy and one round; passive drying is free, conditions-dependent, at most 120 rounds. Balance service 200, wear 0.1 per reading; tray wear 0.01 per actual drying round. Missing energy/tool pauses without charges.
interfaces.effects: Two persistent apparatuses with geometry, inputs, comparison pieces and measured calibration history. Actual sample water changes physical carrying mass; original nutrition/toxin totals remain in food units. Three stable paid readings separated by three actual drying advances produce a relative residue estimate with uncertainty. Visible appearance, residue and negative results never establish safety. Action change cancels active handling and releases the altered ground sample; passive physical drying can continue while it remains on its tray, but supplies no automatic result or reward. Death stops this actor’s remaining assay process once. Partial constructed balance is retained uncalibrated; completing an interrupted assembly after its cancellation requires a new reviewed handling method, never free completion.

execution.progress: Assembly has exact paid stages; drying completion is unknown until real stable measurements. Global checkpoints retain everything. Active handling cannot continue from a different action or position; spent work and water loss are never refunded. Controls use the shared owned-item resolver; exact resolved identities persist for ongoing work.

interfaces.name: Inspect and strip represented bark
interfaces.function: Inspect an actual source or owned material, then strip a finite verified separable layer. Generic branch names do not establish a bark layer.
interfaces.costs: Inspect: one round, 0.2 energy, actual reach <=0.65; tool may be empty. Strip: personal positive inspection, actual supported layer and retained owned stone of hardness >=8; two performed rounds at 0.5 energy each. At most 0.12 mass is removed from substrate in exact representable steps; no material is supplied.
interfaces.effects: Nullable composition stays unknown until actual evidence exists. Finite layer mass and sheet area decline; only completed suitable sheets become bark. Partial/failed material remains bark-fragments. Shared source locks prevent simultaneous gathering or duplicate extraction. No felling, regeneration, free apparatus or guaranteed bark yield.

execution.progress: Inspection completes once; stripping has two paid stages. Lost tools or energy pause without charges. Change of action, loss of reach, destroyed substrate or death cancels once; surviving removed fragments remain, unremoved material remains in the same substrate.

interfaces.name: Tested woven assay supports
interfaces.function: Test real branch and vine batches, fabricate a bark-free comparison balance and mesh from paid components, resume partial work, and calibrate for existing relative food-mass measurements.
interfaces.costs: Tests: target owned branch/vine, controls one hardness>=8 stone, project a new personal ID. Two performed rounds, 0.5 energy each, 0.1 material retained as tested specimen; vine dries passively then needs reachable finite water for real wet comparison. Assembly: personally tested source batches, target 1 branch, controls 3 vine and two distinct hard stones (retained tool first, subdivision second); 12 assembly + 2 subdivision rounds at 0.5 energy. Explicit clear x/y places 0.8 by 0.4 balance, 0.4 by 0.4 mesh at y+0.65, both within 0.65 hand reach. Five real comparison pieces conserve the second stone. Calibration requires personal food-assay mastery, the same project and all original weights, three performed rounds at 0.5 energy. Unused target empty, controls empty. Resume names same own project; controls optionally explicit retained replacement hard tools. No duplicate input or silent substitution.
interfaces.effects: Versioned material laws and paid dry/wet tests record force, geometry, failure and uncertainty. Unknown/failed or insufficient working loads cannot authorize fabrication. Persist component lineage, paid stages and remaining work. Real aperture, sample retention, contact water, tare drift, wear and capacity constrain subsequent food-assay. No composition or safety certification. Action change/death releases only unconsumed surviving escrow once; consumed parts remain in partial apparatus. Resume executes remaining work; destruction yields conserved damaged salvage. Passive drying/creep/wear continue without owner. New grounded information uses existing shared understanding; construction/mastery has no completion reward.

execution.progress: Exact performed stages retained in own project. Passive exposure duration unknown. Missing effort/tool/water pauses without charges; explicit resume locks the same surviving allocations and partial apparatus.

request.name: Physical tool-hardness assessment
request.function: Measure whether an actual owned stone meets the hardness >=8 prerequisite used by bark stripping and assay fabrication, using a physically grounded test rather than inferring hardness from its resource name or load resistance.
request.conditions: I own 0.9 stone in item-61-moss-327. A gentle press at load 0.2 held with flexibility 0, but did not measure hardness. Existing tool-dependent interfaces require hardness >=8.
request.inputs: The owned stone is available. Required comparison materials or equipment are unknown; do not assume they exist.
request.costs: Unknown. Specify finite material use, effort, risks and any prerequisite standards or apparatus.
request.effects: Retain an actual measured result with uncertainty and provenance, or an explicit unresolved result if available materials cannot support the measurement. Do not grant hardness, create standards, or certify suitability without evidence.

projects.question: Can I obtain suitable materials for a calibrated food mass assay?
evidence: Tick 67: a stone pressing trial at load 0.2 held, with measured flexibility 0.
The trial consumed 0.1 stone; 0.9 remains owned.
No stone hardness measurement or suitable bark layer has been established.
projects.uncertainty: Low-load resistance does not establish hardness >=8. Branch suitability, vine availability and reachable finite water remain unverified.
projects.goal: Check material feasibility before committing to fabrication.
completedSteps: Performed a gentle stone pressing trial.
projects.missing: Verified tool hardness and suitable fabrication materials.
projects.next: Replenish known-safe food, then measure the owned branch's gentle load response.
projects.benefit: Established one material response without injury.

projects.question: What internal physical condition can I establish for my stored roots without eating a test sample?
evidence: Tick 24: paid internal examination measured integrity 0.91, soft firmness and little observable deterioration (event-24-moss-132).
The opened 0.1-unit sample was retained; no food was eaten during examination.
projects.uncertainty: This examination does not establish safety, digestibility, calories or toxin absence.
projects.goal: Inspect a small sample of stored roots without ingestion.
completedSteps: Opened and completed internal examination of an owned root sample.
projects.next: Use the measured condition without treating it as a chemical safety test.
projects.benefit: Established internal physical condition without ingestion.

projects.question: What useful physical properties does the nearby wet clay actually exhibit?
evidence: Tick 16 pressing trial consumed 0.1 clay and measured load 0.2, held false, flexibility 0.8 (event-16-moss-82).
projects.uncertainty: Other load bands, wetting, heating and practical applications remain untested.
projects.goal: Perform a gentle pressing trial on the collected clay.
completedSteps: Completed a gentle physical pressing trial.
outputs: Verified low-load response recorded in personal knowledge.
projects.missing: No practical application has been established.
projects.next: Retain the finding; recover energy before further work.
projects.benefit: Established a measured material response without injury.
